exposure: maternal age (categorized as 35-39 years, 40-44 years, >= 45 years)
cohort: The study included full-term pregnant individuals aged 35 years or older who attempted vaginal delivery at a single facility between January 2019 and December 2023.
finding: The risk of intrapartum cesarean delivery increased with maternal age, but full-term deliveries in individuals aged >= 45 years had similar neonatal outcomes to those in younger advanced maternal age pregnancies.
mod_finding: The intrapartum cesarean delivery rate increased significantly with maternal age, though more than half of deliveries were vaginal even in the very advanced maternal age group, and nearly two-thirds of the overall cohort achieved vaginal delivery.
